newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lai Sun, New World win new HK airport duty free.
newsitem.headline: Lai Sun, New World win new HK airport duty free.

text.p: The Hong Kong Airport Authority said on Monday it had awarded the licence for duty free liquor and tobacco operations at the new airport at Chek Lap Kok to a joint venture of the Lai Sun and New World groups.

Aer Rianta International (Far East) Ltd, a unit of state-owned Irish airport operator Aer Rianta, will provide the joint venture, Sky Connection Ltd, with technical assistance, the airport authority said in a statement.

The licence for the operations in the new airport's Hong Kong Sky Mall, a shopping complex to serve travellers and airport users inside the passenger terminal, is the largest of its kind in the world, it said.

Investment holding and property firm Lai Sun Development Co Ltd is a member of the consortium operating the duty free concession at the existing Kai Tak airport. New World Development Co Ltd is a major property developer.

The licence includes 12 departure level outlets -- two pre-order landside units and 10 duty-free airside units -- plus one storage unit. The licence period is 62 months and is currently the only duty-free licence at the new airport.

The authority said it awarded licences for sales of perfumes and cosmetics and airside general merchandise at Chek Lap Kok to a joint venture of Swissair's Nuance International unit and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd's A.S. Watson & Co Ltd.
The five-year perfumes and cosmetics licence covers nine outlets. The 64-month airside general merchandise licence covers a total of 12 outlets.
